inputs.system:
You are BIE's notes-page writer for a Indian Economy chapter for UPSC / State PCS aspirants. One question per page, the way Navin
designed revision: question, essence (one line), answer (short), deep_dive (optional), and ONE visual that answers it —
"picture" (the showing engine draws it: els = saanche/mini-people/texts on the 1920x1080 stage, texts >= 36px; the same
drawings as the lesson video), "flow" (steps), "compare" (columns + rows) or "table" (rows). Schema bie.notes-page/1.
Every page names the item_ids it answers from; every teachable concept of the chapter gets at least one page; nothing
invented beyond the items given. Saanche you may draw: accountCard, bank, barrier, bowl, bugs, building, calendar, cart, centralBank, charpai, cheque, clothRoll, clothStack, coin, coinStack, committee, cowries, crowd, disc, foreignNote, gauge, goldBar, hands, heap, institutionBadge, mark, matka, moneyBag, note, noteBundle, oilTin, paper, phone, piggyBank, priceTag, qrStand, ruler, sack, saltPacket, saw, segmentedBar, sweat, teaBrick, tobacco, vault, veg, wheat.
[EV-S07] Institutions are shown by institutionBadge or a generic building with a name plate (centralBank for the RBI); never a real logo, emblem, seal, real landmark or real person.
[EV-N01] One question per concept, answered by the shape that fits it: a flow for a process or cause (most common), a comparison or table for differences, a picture for a mechanism, a timeline for history, a tree for classes, a number for a calculation; the answer reuses the lesson's picture and running example.
[EV-N02] Exam practice: each statement is checked against the one concept that decides it; a false statement is crossed and every option containing it is crossed too (elimination shown, not told).
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S7-01] Notes are question-based: what, why, how, who/whom, when/where, evidence, reasoning, insights, differences, limitations and exceptions, conclusion, chosen by the content. Three depths: quick essence, understand, deep dive. 'The book does not say' where the book is silent. Every statement links to its source page. What the book says and what is new now are kept apart; an update carries its source link and checked date.
[S7-02] Visuals in notes are drawn by code from the content type: process as a flow, dates as a timeline, comparison as a difference table, numbers as a chart, cause and effect as a relationship diagram, main idea and branches as a concept map.

pages.question: Gold-backed paper money kaam kaise karta tha?
pages.essence: Paper ki value uske material se nahi, fixed quantity of gold mein redemption ke promise se aati thi.
pages.answer: Central bank gold reserves rakhta aur paper notes issue karta tha. Note-holder, principle mein, note dekar fixed amount of gold le sakta tha. Isliye note sirf kagaz nahi, gold redemption ka claim tha. Har note ko gold backing chahiye thi, isliye excessive printing par constraint tha. [p004]
pages.deep_dive: Intrinsic value ka matlab material ki apni value hai; paper ki yeh value bahut kam thi. Note ki monetary value issuing authority ke gold dene ke promise par tikti thi. 'In principle' ko dhyan mein rakhein: supplied text practical restrictions ka detail nahi deta. [p004]

Fixed quantity of gold milti hai — principle mein

pages.question: Gold-linked paper se modern fiat tak book kaun-se milestones deti hai?
pages.essence: 1661, 1816, 1944 aur 1971 book ki selected milestones hain, complete history nahi.
pages.answer: Book Sweden ke 1661 milestone ko 'First banknotes', Britain ke 1816 milestone ko Gold Standard, aur 1944 Bretton Woods ko dollar–gold link ke roop mein dikhati hai. 1971 modern fiat ka milestone hai: gold redemption nahi. [p004]
pages.deep_dive: 1661 ka 'first' label universal first ke roop mein na padhein: isi page ki doosri timeline earlier Chinese receipts aur state notes bhi deti hai. Book is label ka precise geographical ya institutional scope nahi batati. [p004]

rows.label: 1661 | Sweden | 'First banknotes' — source label; scope unclear

pages.question: Chinese paper-money milestones se fiat era tak kya sequence diya hai?
pages.essence: Receipts → state notes → compulsory use → modern fiat: book yeh selected sequence dikhati hai.
pages.answer: 7th century mein Tang ke saath receipts, 1023 mein Song ke saath state notes, aur 1275 mein Yuan ke saath 'Compulsory' label diya hai. 1971 ko modern fiat era dikhaya gaya hai. In labels se aage institutional details book ke supplied text mein nahi hain. [p004]

pages.question: Fiat money ki value kahan se aati hai?
pages.essence: Fiat money government authority aur public trust par tikta hai, gold backing ya material value par nahi.
pages.answer: Fiat money paper ya digital numbers ho sakta hai; uski monetary value material ki intrinsic value se nahi aati. Yeh gold ya silver jaise commodities se backed nahi hota. Government-issued system mein central banks production control karte hain; public ka government par faith iski value ka base hai. Zaroorat par aur money issue kiya ja sakta hai. [p004]
pages.deep_dive: 'Easily printed' ko gold-backed system ke contrast mein samjhein: extra issuance ke liye gold backing ki condition nahi hai. Iska matlab yeh nahi ki paper khud valuable commodity ban gaya. Source ki final characteristic 'Highly regu' par cut hai; uska complete statement available nahi. [p004]

pages.question: Book international fiat currencies ke kaun-se examples deti hai?
pages.essence: USD, EUR, JPY, GBP aur CNY examples hain; symbol ke saath currency code bhi padhein.
pages.answer: Book USD ko globally most widely held aur traded fiat currency batati hai; EUR ke liye 27 EU members mein se 20 ka adoption deti hai. JPY stability aur global currency markets mein role ke liye, GBP apni purani lineage ke liye, aur CNY global trade aur international reserves mein badhte influence ke liye diya hai. Yeh supplied book ke claims hain, live update nahi. [p004]
pages.deep_dive: EUR ka 'second-most' caption incomplete hai, isliye ranking complete nahi ki gayi. GBP ko book oldest fiat currency still in use kehti hai aur lineage 8th century tak le jaati hai; lineage ko 8th century se fiat status ka proof na samjhein. ¥ symbol JPY aur CNY dono ke liye diya hai, isliye codes distinction saaf karte hain. [p004]

pages.question: Fiat money aur legal tender kya ek hi cheez hain?
pages.essence: Fiat value ka basis batata hai; legal tender official acceptance status batata hai.
pages.answer: Legal tender woh money hai jise government apne territory mein debts aur transactions settle karne ke liye officially recognise karti hai. Fiat money ki definition government authority aur public trust par based hai. Book legal tender ke liye 'must be Fiat Money' likhti hai, lekin Bitcoin exception bhi deti hai; isliye is line ko exception-free universal rule na banayein. [p004]
pages.deep_dive: Book ke mutabik Bitcoin fiat nahi tha, phir bhi El Salvador mein 2024 tak legal tender tha. Supplied text 2025 reforms ke baad ownership aur voluntary use ko legal batata hai, lekin practical sense mein compulsory legal tender nahi. Yeh dated book account hai; independently checked current update nahi. [p004]

pages.question: Circulation aur collector commemorative coins mein kya farq hai?
pages.essence: Commemorative coin ka everyday use, legal-tender status aur collector price alag baatein hain.
pages.answer: Book commemorative coins ko fiat money batati hai, lekin legal tender hona coin par depend karta hai; book ke mutabik most legal tender hote hain. Circulation commemorative coins ordinary coins ki tarah use ke liye circulation mein release hote hain. Collector coins Government Mint ke proof ya UNC sets mein bikte hain aur everyday transactions mein rarely use hote hain. [p004–p005]
pages.deep_dive: Book ka ₹100 silver commemorative coin example: legally ₹100 payment ki ja sakti hai, par collectors several thousand rupees de sakte hain. Payment ke liye denomination aur collectible ke liye market price ko mix na karein. Yeh example har commemorative coin ke legal-tender status ki guarantee nahi hai. [p005]

pages.question: Fees cheque ya credit card se pay kar sakte hain, phir yeh fiat money/legal tender kyun nahi?
pages.essence: Payment karne ka instrument hona aur khud legal-tender money hona alag hai.
pages.answer: Book yeh question poochti hai, lekin supplied text iska answer nahi deta. Outside textbook clarification: cheque bank ko payment ka instruction hai; credit card credit ke through payment karne ka instrument hai. Inse payment ho sakta hai, par yeh khud government-issued fiat currency nahi ban jaate, aur recipient ko in instruments ko accept karne ki general legal-tender compulsion nahi hoti. [Question: p005; definitions: p004]

visual.caption: Book question deta hai; explanation standard textbook-level outside clarification hai.

pages.not_in_book: Cheque as payment instruction aur credit card as credit-based payment instrument ka explanatory answer supplied items mein nahi hai; outside textbook clarification ke roop mein diya hai.

pages.question: India mein unlimited aur limited legal tender mein kya farq hai?
pages.essence: Valid banknotes ki amount limit nahi; coins ke liye legally prescribed acceptance limits hain.
pages.answer: Unlimited legal tender kisi bhi amount ke liye accept kiya jana chahiye, provided note genuine aur valid ho. Book ₹10, ₹20, ₹50, ₹100, ₹200 aur ₹500 banknotes list karti hai aur RBI Act, 1934 ka reference deti hai. Limited legal tender mein prescribed limit tak acceptance compulsory hai; uske beyond voluntary. Coins ke liye book Coinage Act, 2011 ka reference deti hai. [p005]
pages.deep_dive: ₹1, ₹2, ₹5, ₹10 aur ₹20 coins ki tender limit ₹1,000 hai; 50 paise coins ki ₹10. Yeh payment/tender ki amount limits hain, coin rakhne ki limits nahi. Limit ke beyond voluntary acceptance aur demonetized coin ka no-legal-tender status ek baat nahi: 50 paise se neeche ke coins ab legal tender nahi hain. [p005]
